item.title: Cervical Rotation SNAG
clinicalUse: Painful/restricted cervical rotation with a clear immediate response
Selected cervicogenic headache presentations after appropriate screening
therapistPosition: Stand slightly behind and to the side.
contact: Thumb/finger contact over the selected articular pillar; reinforce with opposite hand if trained.
forceDirection: Sustained glide in the plane of the facet while patient actively rotates.
Movement must remain pain-free or clearly improved.
dosage: 6–10 repetitions × 1–3 sets if response is positive.
mistakes: Pushing straight anteriorly instead of facet plane.
safety: Stop with dizziness, unusual headache, visual symptoms, neurological change.
item.visualCue: Facet glide sustained + patient rotates → Pain-free gain should persist on retest.

subTechniques.name: Cervical SNAG for Rotation
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve a painful/restricted cervical rotation when a sustained segmental glide makes rotation immediately easier.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting upright with the head in neutral and the painful rotation measured first.
subTechniques.contact: Apply the trained facet-directed contact at the selected segment; the patient's head remains under their own active control.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the segmental glide while the patient actively rotates into the previously limited direction. The movement should be pain-free or clearly improved.
subTechniques.dosage: 6–10 repetitions; repeat 1–3 sets only if improvement is maintained.
subTechniques.reassess: Cervical rotation and the patient's look-over-shoulder task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: A SNAG is movement plus glide; if the patient is passive, it is not a SNAG.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Cervical screening and clinician training are required.

subTechniques.name: Self-SNAG for Cervical Rotation
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Allow the patient to reproduce a helpful pain-free glide independently when they can control the technique safely.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting with a towel/strap positioned exactly as taught by the clinician.
subTechniques.contact: The towel supports the selected segment while the hands guide the direction of the self-glide.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the gentle glide while actively rotating; stop before pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms.
subTechniques.reassess: Pain-free rotation immediately after the self-SNAG.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Teach self-SNAG only after a clinician has confirmed the direction is helpful and the patient can reproduce it correctly.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop with dizziness, unusual headache, visual symptoms or distal neurological change.
